Yes boss, the sky appears blue because of a process called Rayleigh scattering. When sunlight enters Earth's atmosphere, it collides with molecules and small particles in the air. Sunlight is made up of different colors, each with its own wavelength. Blue light waves are shorter and smaller than other colors, so they scatter more easily in all directions by the gases and molecules in the atmosphere. This scattered blue light is what we see when we look up at the sky. The other colors, like red and yellow, have longer wavelengths and scatter less, so they don’t dominate the sky’s appearance. That’s why the sky looks blue during the day.
